correctness.rationale: The generator fibers are exactly {f,f^-1} when a genuine chain exists and the coprime powers of f on its support otherwise. An ambient permutation normalizes the generated inverse submonoid if and only if it maps f to one of these generators. Component centralizers are products of cyclic wreath factors and chain-permutation symmetric groups; global coordinate reversal and simultaneous unit-power coordinate multiplication give homomorphic sections of the normalizer quotient, yielding the stated split semidirect products. Orbit-stabilizer yields the explicit class size for every chain/cycle profile. Exact direct closure and permutation-conjugation enumeration agrees for n=0 through 5; this finite evidence supplements, rather than replaces, the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The claim is limited to full split normalizer isomorphisms, their actions on component centralizers, and exact orbit sizes of embedded inverse submonoids. Araújo–Kinyon–Konieczny (2018) explicitly count element conjugacy classes via bipartitions, Elliott–Levine–Mitchell (2023) count abstract isomorphism types, and the two published later embedded-submonoid studies establish generator rigidity and labelled-profile totals. These known statements are fully credited; they do not state the normalizer group splitting. The present proof calculates and splits the stabilizer beyond the earlier orbit and generator-fiber assertions. A more general unpublished or unindexed normalizer theorem could subsume the formula, so priority remains subject to that residual risk.
residual_risks: An older general theory of normalizers of partial-permutation cyclic subgroups may imply the split normalizer without mentioning monogenic inverse submonoids.
Preston (1986) full article was not inspected; its abstract emphasizes isomorphism-type classification.
Semantic literature indexing and a few relevant full texts do not establish absolute global priority.

value.rationale: The exact symmetry stabilizer is a natural invariant of an embedded inverse submonoid, controlling all of its conjugacy-orbit sizes and quantifying its ambient symmetries. The complete infinite-family classification distinguishes the involutory chain regime from a global cyclic-unit regime, including explicit automorphism actions on the centralizer factors and all boundary cases. Previously known partition counts do not describe this normalizer group or individual orbit sizes, which require the additional split-action analysis.
